title: From Biased Chatbots to Biased Agents: Examining Role Assignment Effects on LLM Agent Robustness
benchmark_measurement: Implicit bias detection in strategic reasoning tasks, measured by performance variations (e.g., accuracy drops or gains) when an LLM agent is assigned a specific religious persona.
findings: Assigning religious personas causes significant and inconsistent performance variations in strategic reasoning tasks. For the DeepSeek V3 model, Christian and Buddhist personas led to dramatic performance drops in a card game, while Jewish and Chinese Traditional personas improved performance. Conversely, GPT-40-mini showed an almost opposite trend. These fluctuations suggest that religious cues interact with model-specific pretraining data and alignment procedures, creating unpredictable behavior and revealing robustness failures.
